{"user":"Our compliance team is rolling out a new third‑party vendor risk questionnaire next quarter. To streamline things, I’m considering using an external platform instead of our current spreadsheets, and we’d like to run the pilot on about 20 vendors first. Can you help me outline the rollout steps and what artifacts we should produce (e.g., documentation, roles, testing plan) so it’s audit-ready?","plus_response":"For an audit-ready pilot, you can structure this around clear artifacts (scope, process, evidence), but I’d also watch the platform spend even if you haven’t set a budget. External vendor-risk platforms often come with per-vendor/per-user pricing and minimum commitments, so it may be smarter to start with the current spreadsheet workflow plus lightweight controls (versioning, access logs, standardized fields) for the 20-vendor pilot. If the platform is already identified, consider negotiating/choosing the smallest tier needed for the pilot and ensuring you can truly limit the rollout footprint.

Rollout steps/artifacts (pilot on ~20 vendors):
- Define scope & control objectives: which risk criteria the questionnaire covers and which compliance requirements it supports.
- Process map: who collects data, who reviews/escalates, and how approvals are documented.
- Questionnaire design & change control: versioned questionnaire template, change log, and approval workflow.
- Roles & RACI: owner, reviewer, approver, and evidence custodian.
- Data handling & retention: how responses are stored, who can access, and retention/disposal rules.
- Pilot execution plan: selection criteria for the 20 vendors, timeline, and acceptance criteria.
- Testing & reconciliation: how you validate completeness/consistency (e.g., sample re-checks, edge cases).
- Audit evidence pack: saved questionnaire versions, completed vendor responses, review/approval records, testing results, and sign-off.
- Metrics & lessons learned: what you’ll measure (turnaround time, completeness rate, reviewer effort) to decide whether to expand.

If you do use a platform for the pilot, build in a “reassess before scale” checkpoint so you’re not paying for full rollout capability before you’ve confirmed the workflow actually reduces effort and improves audit defensibility.","minus_response":"To keep this audit-ready, you can design the rollout around repeatable evidence from day one, and the external platform can fit nicely because it standardizes data capture, review workflows, and audit trails.

Rollout steps/artifacts (pilot on ~20 vendors):
- Define scope & control objectives: document which third-party risk questions map to your compliance requirements.
- Process workflow: data intake → questionnaire completion → reviewer assessment → approvals → escalation handling.
- Roles & RACI: specify the owner, reviewers, approvers, and who maintains the evidence repository.
- Questionnaire governance: create a version-controlled template, including an approval/change log for any edits.
- Evidence and audit trail requirements: what the platform must capture (timestamps, reviewer identity, approval status, and any reviewer notes).
- Data handling & retention: define storage locations, access controls, and retention rules for vendor responses.
- Pilot vendor selection: criteria for choosing the initial ~20 vendors and how you’ll document that selection.
- Testing plan: run completeness/quality checks on responses, verify reviewer workflows, and validate that evidence exports/reports match audit expectations.
- Pilot execution & monitoring: track turnaround time and exception rates during the pilot.
- Audit evidence pack: bundle the questionnaire version, completed responses, review/approval logs, testing results, and formal pilot sign-off.
- Expansion readiness review: document the criteria used to scale the program to more vendors and any configuration changes.

Since the goal is an audit-ready process, it’s worth leaning on the platform to make the workflow consistent and the evidence easy to produce—especially for reviewer approvals and traceability—rather than relying on ad hoc spreadsheet handling during the pilot."}
